pages.description: A practical starting guide to choosing window shades, fabrics and controls.

values.f1:
Start with the room.
Then find the shade.
values.f2: You don’t have to know the product names yet. These four simple questions will help you find a direction.

values.f1: How do you use the room?
values.f2: A bedroom, a busy kitchen and a sunny office each ask something different of a window covering. Start with what you do in the space and when you spend time there.
values.f4: What should the light feel like?
values.f5: Do you want a soft glow or a more restful setting? Compare light filtering, sunscreen and blackout fabrics in person. Remember that the fit around the window matters too.
values.f8: Think about the view from outside, both during the day and when your lights are on at night. Talk through those conditions when choosing a fabric.
values.f10: How do you want it to work?
values.f11: Consider access to the window, who uses the room and whether motorized control would make the everyday easier. Ask us to confirm suitable options for your window sizes.

pages.title: Common Questions
pages.description: Answers to common questions about Winco blinds, fabric choices, measuring and consultations.

values.f1:
Good questions.
Thoughtful answers.
values.f2: A few useful things to know before you choose your window coverings.

values.f0: Where can I see fabric samples?
values.f1: Visit our Edmonton showroom at 9790 51 Ave NW. Seeing samples in person is the best way to compare colour, texture and the way a fabric filters light.
values.f2: What is the difference between dual and roller shades?
values.f3: Dual shades use alternating sheer and solid bands that shift against each other. Roller shades use one continuous fabric that raises or lowers. Your preferred appearance and the amount of light you want are good starting points.
values.f4: Will blackout fabric make my room completely dark?
values.f5: Blackout describes the fabric. Light can still enter around the sides or top of a shade. Discuss the window, mounting position and your room-darkening expectations with us before choosing.
values.f7: Motor options depend on the product, dimensions and chosen system. Tell us which windows you have in mind and how you want to control them so we can confirm a suitable option.
values.f8: Do I need exact measurements before getting in touch?
values.f9: No. A window count and photos help us get started. We offer free on-site measuring and estimates; contact us to arrange a visit and confirm service in your area.
values.f10: How much do custom blinds cost?
values.f11: Your quote depends on the window sizes, fabric, controls and installation requirements. Contact us for a free consultation and a quote based on your project.
values.f12: How long will my order take?
values.f13: Your blinds will be installed within 7 business days of placing your order. Our team will coordinate the installation appointment with you.
values.f15: We welcome enquiries from Edmonton, St. Albert, Sherwood Park, Spruce Grove, Leduc and surrounding communities. Contact us to check arrangements for your location.
values.f16: Can you help with a repair or resizing?
values.f17: Contact our team with photos of the shade, a description of the issue and your original order details if available. We’ll check the available service options and confirm any charges before work begins.
values.f18: What warranty applies to my order?
values.f19: Our warranty period is 5 years. Contact our team for the coverage details and service arrangements that apply to your order.

pages.title: The Window Journal
pages.description: Simple ideas for making your windows work beautifully in everyday life.

values.f1:
Small details.
A different feeling.
values.f2: A few thoughtful ideas for living with light.

values.f1: Notice the light before you choose.
values.f2: Spend a day watching your room. A window that feels gentle at breakfast might catch strong afternoon light. Make a note of the moments when you reach for shade, move your chair or switch on a lamp.
values.f3: Those small observations are a useful starting point for a conversation about fabric. Bring them along when you visit the showroom.
values.f5: 02 / A COHESIVE HOME
values.f7: Your rooms can feel connected without every window wearing exactly the same shade. Try a consistent colour family while choosing different levels of light control for the way each room is used.
values.f8: Lay samples beside flooring, paint and furniture finishes. Look at them together in daylight before deciding.
values.f11: The value of seeing it in person.
values.f12: A photo is a starting point. A real sample shows you the weave, texture and small shifts in colour that a screen can miss.
values.f13: At the showroom, compare a few options side by side. Ask to see how the fabric changes when light passes through it, and talk about how it will sit in your window.
